title: Per-Token Latency Attribution and KV Cache Event Correlator
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement: We currently surface request-level latency and coarse cache hit rates, but teams need per-token attribution that ties latency and cost to specific token emissions and to KV cache access timing. This ticket implements a Correlator service and instrumentation hooks that stitch token emission spans with cache-access events so we can answer: 1) which tokens incurred the majority of latency for a request, 2) how much of that latency is attributable to KV cache misses/hits, and 3) token-level cost impact for billing/optimization.

Goals:
- Add structured trace span types for token emission (span.name=token.emit) and cache events (span.name=kv.access) with a shared correlation id.
- Emit micro-timings (microsecond resolution) for token start/end, kv access start/end, and kernel queue wait where available.
- Build a lightweight Correlator component that consumes trace events, joins token spans with the nearest kv.access events by sequence number and correlation id, and writes enriched rows to the observability events topic for downstream dashboards and cost reconciliation.
- Keep production overhead <3% p99 tail increase for common workloads; sampling strategy for high-volume clients.

Scope/in-scope:
- Runtime hooks in the serving runtime to start/finish token.emit spans and to annotate KV cache calls.
- Minor protocol change to include an optional per-request "token_correlation_seed" (64-bit) to enable deterministic sampling and sharding.
- Correlator consumer (Go) that runs in observability namespace, performs event join, and emits enriched events to BigQuery/ClickHouse (depending on workspace).
- Dashboards: a) per-route token latency waterfall, b) token-level cache-hit impact heatmap, c) bucketed cost-attribution per sample.

Out-of-scope: billing pipeline changes (will provide spec + schema), full request replay tool (follow-up ticket).

Acceptance criteria:
- Instrumented runtime emits token.emit and kv.access spans for at least 90% of requests in the canary region.
- Correlator correctly joins spans in >99.5% of sampled traces in our integration tests.
- Dashboards show token-level latency breakdown for three representative routes and expose a new metric token.kv_miss_latency_ms.
- End-to-end overhead measured and documented; sampling default keeps overhead <3% at p99 for latencies.

Design notes:
- Trace model: token.emit spans carry fields: correlation_seed, request_seq (incrementing per token), token_index, model_version, emission_phase (decode/finish). kv.access spans carry: correlation_seed, access_seq, hit:boolean, backend_latency_us, cache_layer. The Correlator matches token_index ~ access_seq by nearest timestamp within a 5ms window; if multiple matches, prefer hit=true, otherwise mark as ambiguous.
- Sampling strategy: deterministic hashing of correlation_seed + client_id to decide per-request sampling rate (0.1% default, 1% for paid tiers). This enables reproducible sampling across retries.
- Storage: enriched events get written to a partitioned table with schema fields flattened: request_id, correlation_seed, token_index, token_latency_us, kv_hit, kv_latency_us, kernel_wait_us, route, model, timestamp. We will provide both full and aggregated materialized views for dashboards.
- Back-pressure and safety: spans are emitted asynchronously; if the tracing buffer is full we drop token-level spans (fall back to request-level) and emit a trace-drop metric.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype token.emit and kv.access span types in a feature branch of the runtime (rust). Add sampling flag and per-request seed. (2 wks)
2) Minimal Correlator consumer (Go) that reads from observability.events topic and performs join for sampled traces; store output to staging table. (2 wks)
3) Integration tests and synthetic traffic harness that validates join correctness across sequence perturbations. (1 wk)
4) Canary rollout to europe-west1; measure perf and correctness. (2 wks)
5) Add dashboards and alerting; handoff docs for billing. (1 wk)

Risks & trade-offs:
- High cardinality events: storing per-token events inflates events volume. Mitigation: deterministic sampling + pre-aggregation and retention policy (keep raw for 30 days, aggregates 365d).
- Join ambiguity when async KV calls reorder relative to emission; mitigations: 5ms window, prefer hits, log ambiguous joins for manual review.
- Runtime overhead: microsecond timers and additional annotations add overhead; we will use fast-path inline timers (rdtsc/clock_gettime) and allocate spans from a per-thread pool to minimize allocations.

Open decisions:
- Final window for joining token->kv: 5ms vs 10ms (performance test pending).
- Storage backend: ClickHouse preferred for quick ad-hoc queries vs BigQuery for long-term joins. We will support both; initial canonical view in ClickHouse.

Related artifacts:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atl.confluence.com/display/OBS/Token+KV+Correlator+Design
- Prototype PR (runtime hooks): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4182
- Correlator consumer repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/tree/feature/token-correlator
- Synthetic test harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks/tree/token-trace-harness

- Wire up test consumer to staging topic and validate join logic with the harness (owner Priya).
- Draft dashboard wireframes for review with PM and Console UX (owner Maya).
